text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT PAGE -> oncall @devon. Severity: P2. Source: Redis Cloud (eu-west) degradation impacting rate-limiter and cache tiers. Please ack and join thread.

devon: acked. jumping in. seeing spikes on gateway 5xx. paging details attached to the PD ticket.

maria: confirmed. API gateway shows surge of `rate_limiter` 503s starting ~03:05 UTC. downstream Redis client errors: connection refused / IO errors.

maria: sample logs from gateway (truncated):
```
2024-06-18T03:06:12Z ERROR rate_limiter: redis error: ERR: IOERR: connection closed
2024-06-18T03:06:13Z WARN  rate_limiter: fallback miss, backend code=503
2024-06-18T03:06:14Z ERROR api-proxy: upstream token-check failed status=503
```

devon: quick impact summary from metrics:
- rate_limiter_rejects +1200/s (peaked)
- cache_hit_rate dropped from 92% -> 30% for eu-west
- customer 5xx count +18% overall, eu-west +60%

devon: initial mitigation plan (in order):
1) Enable local in-memory fallback for rate-limiter (fail-open for token checks) -> reduces customer-facing 503s.
2) Temporarily relax enforcement for non-critical tiers (free/experimental) so we don't block prod traffic.
3) Increase retry/backoff for Redis client with jitter.
4) Open vendor escalation with Redis Cloud and request ETA for region recovery.
5) Notify support and customer success with impact summary and suggested messaging.

priya: I'm enabling memcache fallback now on the canary cluster (eu-west-1). Doing `kubectl patch` to switch config flag `RATE_LIMITER_FALLBACK=memcache` for canary pods.

ops-bot: deploy started: roll/canary(3/3) rate-limiter-fallback -> memcache (k=eu-west-canary). Logs will stream here.

maria: after canary switch we saw 60% reduction in 503s on canary. rolling to remaining pods.

sasha-support: drafting public support blurb: "We are investigating elevated errors for requests served from EU region due to a third-party cache provider incident. Some requests may experience retries or delays. If you see persistent errors, please reach out to support." Want to include affected window and mitigation steps.

devon: vendor update: Redis Cloud status shows an ongoing incident in eu-west affecting managed clusters. Vendor incident ID `RC-2024-06-18-09`. They report degraded control-plane and connection instability. We have open ticket (#78910) and escalated to on-shift account manager.

maria: action taken checklist (performed):
- [x] canary memcache fallback enabled
- [x] rollout memcache fallback to all eu-west pods (rolled in 6min)
- [x] retries/backoff patched in runtime to 3 attempts with exp backoff
- [x] relaxed strict rate limits for tier=free and tier=trial (fail-open)
- [x] PD ticket created and vendor escalated
- [x] support blurb drafted

devon: customer impact assessment (short):
- Impacted surfaces: rate limiting, user-session cache lookups, a small subset of short-lived token caches.
- Likely customer-visible symptoms: transient 5xx for API calls, longer tail latency, occasional duplicate requests due to retries.
- Approx traffic affected: ~15-20% of global traffic (concentrated in eu-west) during incident window.
- Critical customers: two Dedicated customers (EU clusters) reported increased error rates via monitoring; support team reached out proactively.

priya: support please hold on sending the public blurb for 10 minutes so we can confirm rollout fully stabilizes. If stable, send with tags: #eu, #partial-degradation, ETA unknown.

sasha-support: will hold. prepping targeted messages to affected enterprise contacts now.

devon: live mitigation notes:
- Fallback to memcache reduces per-token correctness risk by a small margin (stale tokens possible for ~30s TTL differences). We accepted this trade to avoid mass 503s.
- Rate limiter will operate in degraded mode until vendor confirms full recovery; strict penalties re-enabled post-incident with rollout monitor.

maria: current realtime metrics (after full rollout):
- 5xx delta down from +60% -> +6% in eu-west
- cache hit rate back up to ~78%
- request latency still ~12% above baseline due to retries

pagerduty-bot: REMINDER -> Please update PD ticket with each major step.

devon: handoff plan: I'm going offline for 30m at 04:20 UTC for a hard stop. @priya, can you take primary until vendor declares resolved? If anything degrades, contact me on phone.

priya: I have it. I'll keep an eye for regressions and vendor updates. Will escalate to ESC if Redis Cloud ETA > 2hrs.

sasha-support: public post ready once priya confirms stable for 10m. Draft below: 
"Update: We experienced degraded service in our EU region due to an incident with our managed cache provider. We have applied mitigations to restore service and reduce errors. Some customers may experience transient delays or retries. We will update this thread as the vendor provides more information."

ops-bot: vendor ticket updated: #78910 -> status: escalated to engineering on-call at Redis Cloud. Contact: emea-ops@redislabs.example (via vendor).

devon: closing notes for now (will follow up when vendor confirms full resolution):
- Mitigations reduced customer-facing errors significantly; primary customer impact is increased latency and occasional stale cache values within TTL windows.
- Postmortem owners: eng-runtime (maria), eng-sre (devon), support (sasha-support).
- Immediate follow-ups: verify rollback plan to strict limits, add automated switch to fallback earlier when Redis error rate > X, and add vendor-health monitor to our dashboards.

priya: marking thread as active and monitoring. will post final vendor confirmation and downtime window when available.

sasha-support: note for CS: two Dedicated customers already notified proactively, waiting for their feedback; we'll queue any billing/SLAs questions until incident postmortem.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED -> severity remains P2.

priya: vendor just posted note: partial connectivity restored as of 04:15 UTC. they are validating data-plane and will post full recovery. I'll leave this thread open until we see 30m of stable metrics.

maria: fine-by-me. monitoring continues.

devon: thanks team. great job moving fast on fallback.

priya: (handoff) taking over monitoring. will update with final resolution.

[thread will remain open for postmortem and timeline entries]
